newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament allows trial of ex-customs chief.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament allows trial of ex-customs chief.

text.p: Poland's parliament on Friday lifted the immunity of a ruling ex-communist party deputy to allow his prosecution in a customs service corruption scandal.

Ireneusz Sekula is to be charged for an allegedly improper property deal he made as head of customs in what opposition parties have said was evidence of widespread sleaze among ex-communists in power.

Sekula had himself asked for his parliamentary immunity to be removed, saying he could prove in court he was fully justified. His own party supported the motion which passed by 346 to 4 votes with 11 abstentions.

Prosecutors accuse Sekula, sacked last year as head of the Main Customs Office (GUC), of buying an inappropriate office building from trading company Universal SA for much more than it was worth and needlessly paying a large sum in advance.
Critics say the state suffered serious losses and question Sekula's motives in going ahead against advisers' objections.
Sekula's Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), main party in the ruling coalition, was born out of the old communist party after it was toppled in 1989, and which went on to win 1993 elections.
Last year the party voted to uphold Sekula's immunity when he faced other allegations relating to a trading company he headed that went bankrupt.
SLD leaders said before Friday's vote that they had now agreed to let him be prosecuted over the customs office issue because they were sure he could clear his name.
"Besides, by voting against removing his immunity, the SLD suffered major political harm," the party's parliamentary leader Jerzy Szmajdzinski told Gazeta Wyborcza newspaper.
Campaigning is getting underway for parliamentary elections due next year.
